summary: Current 54-ft steel tower and CL-100 cab built 1959 on Barillas Peak; earlier lookouts date from before 1920; on the Register since 2007; standing, staffing undated.

facts.design: 54-foot steel tower with a 14-by-14-foot live-in CL-100 type cab and catwalk; the Register and the 2020 report call the tower an Aermotor

access.note: No current public-access rule in the sources read; Zinn says a road reached the summit by late 1958

events.note: Earliest tower on the peak was an old U.S. Weather Bureau tower erected prior to 1920 (Zinn); NHLR instead says the first lookout was a 7x7 ft metal cab built in the 1930s
Fire began April 15, 1925 at the Reid Sawmill below Barillas, burned over the peak; the tower was apparently saved
Lookout cabin completed in 1926 after the Forest budgeted for it in 1925; 2015 tree-ring dating of logs fits the late 1920s
Enclosed metal cab, only about 4 by 4 feet, on a 30-foot metal tower by 1928 (Zinn)
Regional Office decided to abandon Barillas in 1949 instead of building a road and new tower; old tower had been condemned in the late 1940s
Commissary Fire started June 6, 1950 below the abandoned lookout; Board of Review said a guard on the peak might have held it down
Barillas reopened as an emergency lookout using the old cabin and three map boards
Forest completed the road from Lower Colonias to the summit by late 1958
Current 54-ft steel tower with 14x14 CL-100 type cab completed November 1959; NHLR and the 2020 report also date it to 1959
Old tower dismantled when the new one was built; its cab was left on the ground
Tony Vigil was the first to staff the new lookout
Cat and Dog Fire burned through the Barillas area; lookout had to be evacuated
Cab left on the ground removed for scrap after the 1971 fire, then became a playhouse in East Pecos (Zinn); Zinn also places the original cab on private land west of Barillas
Gail Roos and Rich Rydin were the Barillas lookouts
Richard Martinez staffed Barillas full-time during the summers of 1982 and 1983
Polly Mullen worked at Barillas for part of the extreme fire season; crew remodeled the interior with donated materials later that season
Placed on the National Historic Lookout Register on December 7, 2007
Managed Commissary Fire burned 2,500 acres just south of the lookout
Evaluated for the 1988 thematic National Register nomination and found not eligible due to age
2020 New Mexico chapter report recommends the lookout be re-evaluated for the National Register

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR says the first Barillas Lookout was a 7x7 ft metal cab built in the 1930s. Zinn describes an old Weather Bureau tower erected before 1920 and a 4x4 ft enclosed cab on a 30-ft tower by 1928, with dated inspections. The story follows Zinn and notes the mismatch.
The Register and the 2020 report say Aermotor; Zinn calls the 1959 tower a steel tower and names no maker. These do not contradict each other.

sources.title: Fire Lookout History of the Santa Fe National Forest (Barbara Zinn)

notes_for_editor: Built 1959 date agrees across NHLR, the 2020 report and Zinn; the earlier history rests on Zinn's chapter, which dates its sources. Conflict: NHLR's 1930s first-lookout claim does not match Zinn. Unresolved: Zinn places the original 1928 cab on private land west of the peak, but also says the cab left at the site was scrapped and became a playhouse in East Pecos. Current status rests on the undated NHLR page ('Staffed? No', condition good) and the FFLA state list; no 2024-2026 source was read. Access is unverified. A 2022 FFLA Facebook post in search results (not read, not used) says the Calf Canyon/Hermits Peak fire came close to the lookout. The old cabin demolition date is only 'late 1960s'. The 1988 thematic nomination and any NRHP nomination on npgallery were not read.
